## 1. Purpose

This procedure describes the classification, segregation, labeling,
storage, and disposal of all laboratory waste generated in EA Program
laboratories, with emphasis on hazardous chemical waste requiring
EH&S pickup. It consolidates and expands the waste disposal sections
of [SOP-L003 Hazardous Materials Handling](SOP-L003-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd)
(Sections 8.1--8.6) into a standalone reference that can be posted in
the waste accumulation area and used during training.


## 2. Scope

- **Applies to:** All laboratory waste generated in EA Program
  laboratories (SGM 133, 134, 135), including chemical waste,
  biological waste, sharps, and non-hazardous solid waste
- **Does not apply to:** Radioactive waste (not generated in EA
  Program labs); field waste (see
  [SOP-F001](../field_sops/SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd)); e-waste and
  surplus equipment (coordinate with campus surplus property office)
- **Location:** All EA Program laboratory spaces


## 3. Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                              |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------|
| Lab PI            | Ensure compliance with campus and regulatory waste policies; sign manifests as generator |
| Lab Manager       | Coordinate EH&S pickups, maintain satellite accumulation areas, train personnel |
| All Lab Personnel | Segregate and label waste correctly per this SOP |
| Campus EH&S       | Collect hazardous waste, prepare manifests, arrange off-site disposal |


## 4. Regulatory Context

Pomona College is classified as a Small Quantity Generator (SQG) of
hazardous waste under RCRA (40 CFR Part 262) and California DTSC
regulations. Key requirements:

- Hazardous waste may be accumulated in satellite accumulation areas
  (SAAs) near the point of generation in containers of 55 gallons or
  less (1 quart for acutely hazardous waste)
- Once full, containers must be moved to the central accumulation area
  and picked up by EH&S within 3 days
- All containers must be labeled with the words "Hazardous Waste,"
  the contents, the hazard(s), and the accumulation start date
- The generator (Lab PI) must sign the packing manifest


## 5. Waste Classification

### 5.1 Non-Hazardous Solid Waste

| Waste Type                    | Disposal                                 |
|:------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Paper, packaging, cardboard   | Recycling bins                           |
| Uncontaminated gloves and wipes | Standard trash                         |
| Clean glassware (broken)      | Sharps box or wrapped cardboard, then trash |
| Uncontaminated soil (dried)   | Standard trash or return to field site   |
| Used aluminum tins (clean)    | Recycle or reuse                         |

### 5.2 Hazardous Chemical Waste

Any waste that is ignitable, corrosive, reactive, or toxic (per RCRA
D-list), or that is a listed waste (F, K, P, or U list), must be
collected and disposed as hazardous waste. Common EA Program
hazardous waste streams:

| Waste Stream                  | Typical Source SOPs             | Container                     |
|:------------------------------|:--------------------------------|:------------------------------|
| Acid waste (HNO~3~, HCl, H~2~SO~4~) | L410, L411, L403       | Poly carboy, labeled "Acid Waste" |
| Base waste (NaOH, KOH)       | Various                         | Separate poly carboy          |
| Halogenated solvent waste (chloroform, DCM) | L409              | Amber glass, labeled "Halogenated Solvent Waste" |
| Non-halogenated solvent waste (acetone, ethanol, hexane) | Various | Separate glass or poly container |
| Heavy metal solutions (Pb, Cd, Cr, Hg) | L410, L411            | Poly carboy, labeled by metal |
| Formaldehyde solutions        | L305 (preservatives)           | Glass, labeled "Formaldehyde Waste" |
| Oxidizer solutions (H~2~O~2~, NaClO~3~) | L412               | Collect separately; do not mix with organic waste |
| Used oil (pump oil)           | Vacuum pumps                    | Labeled container             |

::: {.callout-warning}
### Critical Segregation Rules

- **Never mix** acids with bases, oxidizers with organics, or
  halogenated with non-halogenated solvents.
- **Never pour** hazardous waste down the drain unless explicitly
  approved by EH&S for that specific waste stream.
- When in doubt, treat as hazardous and collect for EH&S pickup.
:::

### 5.3 Biological Waste

| Waste Type                    | Disposal                                 |
|:------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Non-pathogenic cultures (soil microbes) | Autoclave, then standard trash |
| Colilert/Quanti-Tray materials (L305) | Standard trash after UV deactivation or autoclave |
| eDNA extraction waste (bead tubes, filters) | Standard trash (non-infectious after extraction) |
| Foreign soil waste (L015)     | Autoclave per SOP-L015 before disposal   |

### 5.4 Sharps

| Waste Type                    | Disposal                                 |
|:------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Needles, syringes with needles | Sharps container (red)                  |
| Broken glass (contaminated)   | Sharps container                         |
| Razor blades, scalpels        | Sharps container                         |
| Broken glass (uncontaminated) | Cardboard box labeled "Broken Glass," then trash |
| Intact glass vials (uncontaminated) | Rinse and recycle, or trash       |

### 5.5 Drain-Disposable Waste

A limited set of aqueous, non-hazardous solutions may be poured down
the drain with copious water, **only if approved by EH&S**:

- Dilute (less than 1%) salt solutions (NaCl, KCl, K~2~SO~4~,
  Na~2~SO~4~) at neutral pH
- Dilute sugar or buffer solutions at neutral pH
- Neutralized acid or base solutions (pH 5--9) that contain no metals
  or other hazardous constituents

::: {.callout-important}
If you are unsure whether a waste can go down the drain, collect it
as chemical waste. The default is always to collect, never to drain.
:::


## 6. Procedure

### 6.1 Labeling Waste Containers

1. Every waste container in the SAA must have a hazardous waste label
   (available from EH&S or the lab manager) before any waste is added
2. Fill in: waste description (chemical names and approximate
   percentages), hazard(s) (corrosive, flammable, toxic, etc.),
   accumulation start date, and laboratory location
3. Update the label if new constituents are added to the container

### 6.2 Accumulating Waste

1. Add waste to the appropriate labeled container in the SAA
2. Keep containers closed when not actively adding waste
3. Do not fill containers beyond 80% capacity (leave headspace for
   thermal expansion and safe handling)
4. Inspect containers weekly for leaks, corrosion, or label
   degradation

### 6.3 Requesting EH&S Pickup

1. When a container is full (or the study is complete), notify the
   lab manager
2. The lab manager contacts campus EH&S to schedule a pickup
3. Prepare a packing manifest listing: container number, contents
   (chemical names and approximate percentages), volume, hazard
   class, and generator (PI) name
4. The PI reviews and signs the manifest
5. Move the container to the central pickup area designated by EH&S
6. EH&S collects the waste, provides a manifest copy, and arranges
   off-site treatment or disposal

### 6.4 Empty Container Management

1. Triple-rinse empty reagent bottles with the appropriate solvent
   (water for aqueous chemicals, the same solvent for organic
   chemicals)
2. Remove or deface the original label
3. Collect rinse liquid as waste (add to the corresponding waste
   stream)
4. Clean, delabeled glass bottles may be reused for non-critical
   purposes or recycled
5. Do not reuse containers that held acutely hazardous (P-listed)
   chemicals; dispose as hazardous waste


## 7. Satellite Accumulation Area (SAA) Management

- Each SAA is located at or near the point of waste generation (e.g.,
  the fume hood where digestions are performed, the bench where
  extractions occur)
- Maximum volume in an SAA: 55 gallons of hazardous waste (or 1 quart
  of acutely hazardous waste)
- Containers in the SAA must be in good condition, compatible with
  the waste, and kept closed except when adding waste
- Spill containment (secondary tray) is required under all liquid
  waste containers
- The lab manager inspects SAAs monthly and logs the inspection on
  the SAA checklist posted in each area


## 8. Emergency Spill Response

For waste container spills, follow
[SOP-L004 Chemical Spill Response](SOP-L004-chemical-spill-response.qmd).
Key points:

- Contain the spill using absorbent materials appropriate to the
  waste type (do not use paper towels for solvent spills; use
  chemical absorbent pads)
- Contaminated absorbent becomes hazardous waste; bag, label, and
  include in the next EH&S pickup
- Report all spills to the lab manager and PI; document in the
  incident log

## 11. Training Record

Before handling laboratory waste independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP and
   [SOP-L003](SOP-L003-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd) in full
2. Locate the SAAs in each laboratory room and identify the waste
   streams currently in use
3. Demonstrate proper waste labeling (fill out a hazardous waste label
   correctly)
4. Demonstrate correct segregation by assigning 5 sample waste items
   to the correct container
5. Review the spill response procedure in
   [SOP-L004](SOP-L004-chemical-spill-response.qmd)
6. Be signed off by the lab manager or PI
